newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian security forces prepare for clashes.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian security forces prepare for clashes.

text.p: Palestinian police and security forces have been told to prepare for a possible confrontation with Israeli soldiers, according to an internal memo of the Palestinian National Forces issued on Monday.

"We call on all security forces to prepare for the worst possibilities. We have to be prepared at all levels without any exceptions because the battle is to be or not to be," said a copy of the memo seen by Reuters.

"We are not waiting for any positive things from the current Israeli government and from the occupation forces in general. We have to wait and see the Israeli military measures and to be warned against any confrontation," it added.
But Major General Abdel Razek al-Majaideh, who commands forces in the northern Gaza Strip, told Reuters:
"There is no state of mobilisation. This is only an internal memo for our security forces to be prepared for any eventuality that might disrupt the peace process by people opposed to the peace deals.
"You know we have opposition and there is an exceptional situation so we are asking our security forces to be on alert and prepared to save the peace process."

Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine, in September led to violent clashes in the West Bank and Gaza in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed.

On Sunday Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said the peace process was "facing real dangers" His statement followed moves by the right-wing Israeli government to expand Jewish settlements in the West Bank.
Asked if the current situation would lead to a revival of the Palestinian uprising, Arafat told the London-based al-Hayat newspaper: "All options are possible."
